Helprise is an organization that combines global reach with local talent. We work for companies that value quality, partnership, and responsibility, creating teams that really work. By precisely matching skills and business needs, we connect specialists with projects where their knowledge has a real impact. By joining us, you become part of an environment where matching is not a coincidence, but a decision.

Today, we are looking for an experienced Fleet Manager to oversee the company’s fleet operations, ensuring cost efficiency, compliance, high service quality, and a positive employee experience.

YOU WILL

  • Manage the end-to-end vehicle lifecycle, including ordering, leasing, maintenance, insurance, and replacement.
  • Manage relationships with leasing companies, suppliers, dealerships, and service providers.
  • Monitor fleet costs, budgets, utilization, and performance KPIs.
  • Negotiate contracts and commercial terms with external partners.
  • Ensure fleet compliance with legal, safety, insurance, and company requirements.
  • Manage fleet policies and provide support to employees on fleet-related matters.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize costs, processes, and fleet efficiency.
  • Support sustainability initiatives, including fleet electrification.
  • Prepare regular fleet reports and analyses.
  • Collaborate with Finance, Procurement, HR, Legal, and other internal stakeholders.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in fleet, mobility, automotive operations, procurement, or a related field.
  • Strong knowledge of fleet operations, leasing, and vehicle lifecycle management.
  • Experience in supplier management and contract negotiation.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Proactive, solution-oriented approach.
  • Fluent English — mandatory.
  • German and/or French — a strong plus.
  • Good Excel and reporting skills; experience with fleet management systems is an advantage.

Benefits

Work flexibility
We give you the opportunity to adjust your work to your lifestyle. We offer flexible hours as well as the possibility of remote or hybrid work, depending on the role and your preferences.

Various forms of cooperation
At Helprise, you can choose the model that best suits your needs. We offer both employment contracts and flexible B2B cooperation options.

Basic benefits package
We care about the health and well-being of our employees - we provide private medical care, a MultiSport card, and life insurance.

Development on your terms
We provide an individual development budget that you can use for your professional growth. As a Lumina Learning partner, we also give you access to unique tools and the support of certified practitioners, so you can better understand your potential and strengthen your talents.

Integration and shared experiences
We regularly enjoy new experiences together and build relationships in an inspiring atmosphere. From cooking sessions, through yoga weekends in nature, to the thrill of escape rooms.

Summary:

The Director, Fleet Safety and Compliance, will ensure that a safe, efficient and legally compliant fleet (including passenger vehicles and transits as well as Commercial Motor Vehicles and emergency response assets) is maintained for the benefit of ASPCA employees and responders as well as the animals we serve. Safely transporting animals throughout the United States is a critical part of ASPCA work and ensuring fleet safety and compliance allows employees at the ASPCA to confidently work to achieve the ASPCA mission and serve the animals in our care.

Who We Are

The ASPCA’s Legal Department helps the ASPCA to achieve its organizational goals of preventing animal cruelty by assessing and managing risk. The Legal Department prioritizes respect for our internal clients, business partners, colleagues and others; excellence in the work that we perform and the advice that we provide; and active engagement in the life-saving work of the ASPCA by showing up for our colleagues, clients, and constituents.

What You’ll Do

The Director, Fleet Safety and Compliance is responsible for leading the development, implementation and continuous improvement of ASPCA’s fleet safety and compliance strategy across all program teams, mobile clinics and field deployments. This role ensures compliance with federal, state and local regulations related to all ASPCA vehicles and drivers while working to identify potential safety risks, to provide innovative approaches and systems that create a safe and compliant fleet and strengthen a culture of safety across the ASPCA. The Director will identify and develop training for ASPCA drivers and support in the review and response of any incidents involving the ASPCA fleet. This role will manage internal, cross-functional relationships and third party vendors needed to support fleet safety and compliance programs.

Director, Fleet Safety and Compliance reports directly to the Vice President, Safety and has no direct reports.

Where and When You’ll Work

  • This remote-based position (which requires travel, as described below) is open to all eligible candidates based within the United States.
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 30% annually, as needed, such that you can visit each ASPCA facility at least once during each calendar year and more, as needed.
  • Periodically serve as a weekend on-call member of the Safety Team in rotation with other members of the Safety Team.

What You’ll Get

Compensation

The target hiring range is based on where the employee works, which for remote roles is the

employee’s primary location of residence, and its respective cost of labor. You can view which zone applies to you based on your location (aspca.app.box.com/v/aspcazonetable). For questions regarding locations not on the list, please send an email to for more information.

Starting pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of factors, including but not limited to education, training, experience, location, business needs, internal equity, market demands or budgeted amount for the role. The target hiring range is for new hire offers only, and compensation may increase beyond the maximum hiring range based on performance over time. The maximum of the hiring range is reserved for candidates with the highest qualifications and relevant experience. The expected hiring salary ranges for this role are set forth below and may be modified in the future.

  • Zone 1: $101,000 – $107,000 annually
  • Zone 2: $111,000 – $117,000 annually
  • Zone 3: $122,000 – $129,000 annually

Benefits

At the ASPCA, you don’t have to choose between your passion and making a living. Our comprehensive benefits package helps ensure you can live a rewarding life at work and at home. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Affordable health coverage, including medical, employer-paid dental, and optional vision coverage.
  • Flexible time off that includes vacation time, sick and bereavement time, paid parental leave, 10 company paid holidays, and paid personal time off that allows you even more flexibility to observe the days that mean the most to you.
  • Competitive financial incentives and retirement savings including a 401(k) plan with generous employer contributions — we match dollar for dollar up to 4% and provide an additional 4% contribution toward your future each year.
  • Robust professional development opportunities including classes, on-the-job training, coaching and mentorship with industry-leading peers, internal mobility, opportunities to support in the field, and so much more.

For more information on our benefits offerings, visit our website.

Responsibilities:

Responsibility buckets are listed in general order of importance, and include but are not limited to:

Fleet Compliance Management

  • Review Electronic Logging Device logs, temperature logs and other reports to assist with compliance and training. Update and reconcile devices for ASPCA assets.
  • Coordinate with Fleet Management Team to ensure regular and preventative maintenance is being performed on all assets according to applicable schedules. Work closely with People Team and Legal Team to ensure that adequate and current safety standards are reflected and maintained in all equipment.
  • Coordinate with Fleet Management Team in the review of all purchase requests for vehicles to promote collaboration with program teams to identify vehicles types most conducive to efficient and safe operations.
  • Manage all DOT filings and reports related to ASPCA fleet vehicles. Identify, assess and mitigate other compliance issues such as federal vehicle/fuel mandates, state laws and Executive Orders.
  • Coordinate with ASPCA colleagues and teams to ensure the collection of all necessary information for, and to draft reports and responses to, federal, state and local compliance audits or inquiries on fleet safety and compliance.

Driver Training and Management

  • Regularly update and reconcile list of active drivers with all departments throughout the organization. Monitor all upcoming registrations and expiration for driver files and licensing.
  • Ensure all Driver Qualification Files are complete and current with all required documentation, including, but not limited to, internal acknowledgements and DOT required documentation. Manage all DOT filings and reports related to ASPCA drivers.
  • Coordinate with People Team to help organize compliance regarding Commercial Drivers Licenses, DOT Medical Cards, and other documentation as required by law.
  • Review monthly Motor Vehicle Record reports and address any deficiencies.
  • Educate drivers and fleet coordinators on state and federal regulations for commercial vehicles traveling throughout the United States.
  • Review and, as necessary, assist the People Team and Legal Team in the investigation of, any accident or incident involving ASPCA drivers. Work to create or improve accident report documentation that is efficient and compliance with applicable law.

Strategy and Engagement

  • Develop best practices for safety and compliance protocols for the ASPCA fleet program and spearhead initiatives related to best practices. Create and improve ASPCA fleet related documents and protocols related to safety and compliance.
  • Effectively communicate and develop partnerships and good relationships with key stakeholders in the organization to achieve and maintain compliance and enhance an organizational culture of health and safety.
  • Develop, foster, and maintain key stakeholder relationships, such as with interconnected government entities, control agencies, outside vendors, and service providers related to fleet safety and compliance.
  • Orchestrate development and dissemination of training and resources on fleet safety and compliance practices and protocols in conjunction with ASPCA colleagues and teams.
  • Support with annual budget and forecasting related to fleet safety and compliance.
  • Participate as a key member of any ASPCA Vehicle and Transport Safety Committee.

Qualifications

  • Strong knowledge of existing governing laws and regulations, including the Department of Transportation (DOT), and emerging guidance promulgated by federal and state agencies regarding fleet safety and compliance required.
  • Proven ability to develop, implement and continuously improve fleet safety and compliance programs across multi-site operations
  • Ability to design and deliver organization-wide fleet safety and compliance training programs
  • Strong written and oral communication skills with the ability to present complex information clearly to diverse audiences
  • Ability to manage projects, including demonstrated reliability, follow-through, meeting deadlines, time management, and managing multiple priorities
  • Proficient in Word, Excel and PowerPoint required
  • Ability to collaborate cross-departmentally and cross-functionally
  • Ability to drive fleet vehicles up to 26,000 pounds as needed in support of fleet management and training
  • Able to provide a valid driver’s license upon hire and pass a motor vehicle history check demonstrating a safe driving history
  • Able to obtain and provide a Department of Transportation Medical Certificate
  • Willing and able to provide all documentation necessary to complete a Driver Qualification File pursuant to DOT and FMCSA requirements in order to drive a Commercial Motor Vehicle with a GVWR of 26,000 pounds or less.
  • Ability to exemplify ASPCA’s core values and behavioral competencies

Education and Work Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience preferred
  • 4 years of professional level fleet safety and compliance experience, including management of Commercial Motor Vehicles and Commercial Drivers License drivers, required
  • Experience overseeing animal transport preferred
  • Experience developing and maintaining fleet safety management systems and compliance documentation required
  • Experience drafting protocols preferred
  • Experience developing and presenting training sessions to be delivered in-person and virtually, preferred
  • Experience partnering with other teams within an organization (e.g. Legal, Human Resources, Facilities and operational teams) on fleet safety and compliance and safety-related issues preferred
  • 5 years of driving experience preferred

Language:

English (Required)

Education and Work Experience:

Bachelors

Are you committed to community safety? We work hard to protect clients, customers, and teammates from fire hazards by installing, maintaining, and inspecting fire suppression systems. Our fire suppression systems ensure uninterrupted operations in businesses you likely visit, and our technicians take pride in their communities, prioritizing safety for all. If you share this passion and commitment, let's talk about how you can join us in our mission and build your future with us!

Position Summary

The Fleet Manager owns both the strategic planning and day to day execution of Marmic's vehicle fleet of approximately 1,200 vehicles operating out of branch locations across the country. This includes vehicle acquisition and lease versus buy strategy, preventive maintenance and driver scheduling, fuel efficiency and cost reduction, DOT and registration compliance, insurance and claims management, fleet safety, and reporting on fleet performance and budgets. The role also owns the accuracy of fleet data across all systems, including Enterprise Fleet Management and the company's Geotab telematics platform. Given the size and geographic spread of the fleet, the role requires strong systems discipline and the ability to coordinate consistent processes across many locations. The Fleet Manager partners closely with Supply Chain, Finance, HR, and branch operations leadership to ensure the fleet supports business needs safely, efficiently, and cost effectively.


Core Responsibilities

The Fleet Manager is accountable for both the strategy and the hands-on execution of each of the following areas:

Vehicle Acquisition & Lifecycle Strategy

  • Develop and execute the company's vehicle acquisition strategy, including lease versus buy analysis, vehicle specification, and replacement cycle planning.
  • Partner with Enterprise Fleet Management and Supply Chain leadership on the purchasing, leasing, and disposal of vehicles to optimize total cost of ownership.
  • Forecast future vehicle needs based on business growth, replacement cycles, and branch requirements, and partner with Supply Chain and Finance leadership on vehicle procurement and capital planning.

Fleet Data & Systems Management

  • Maintain and manage the vehicle status list within Enterprise Fleet Management, ensuring vehicle assignments, in service and out of service status, and vehicle details are accurate and current at all times.
  • Administer the company's Geotab telematics program, including device installation coordination, GPS and diagnostic monitoring, driver behavior reporting, and troubleshooting of device issues.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact with Enterprise Fleet Management and Geotab account representatives, escalating and resolving issues as needed.

Maintenance, Driver Operations & Cost Efficiency

  • Develop and execute a preventive maintenance strategy and scheduling program across the fleet, coordinating repairs to minimize vehicle downtime.
  • Oversee driver scheduling and supervision in coordination with branch leadership, ensuring adequate vehicle availability and coverage across all locations.
  • Develop and execute fuel efficiency and cost reduction strategies across the fleet, monitoring fuel spend and identifying opportunities for savings.

Insurance & Claims Management

  • File and manage all vehicle insurance claims from first notice of loss through final resolution, coordinating with insurance carriers, adjusters, branch managers, and repair vendors.
  • Maintain and update all vehicle insurance information and documentation, including certificates of insurance, VIN schedules, and policy records, ensuring accuracy to support insurance audits and renewals.
  • Track claim status, costs, and outcomes, and identify trends to inform safety and risk mitigation efforts.

Registration, Licensing & Regulatory Compliance

  • Maintain current vehicle tags and registrations in partnership with ABS, ensuring timely renewals and compliance with state DMV requirements across all jurisdictions.
  • Maintain the company's toll tag program, including transponder assignment and inventory, and reconcile monthly toll billing across the fleet.
  • Ensure fleet-wide compliance with U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations and other applicable federal, state, and local transportation requirements.

Fleet Safety Program

  • Own and continuously develop Marmic's fleet safety program, including driver safety policies, motor vehicle record (MVR) monitoring, accident review and root cause analysis, and driver safety training.
  • Partner with HR and branch leadership to address at risk driving behavior identified through telematics data and incident reports.

Metrics, Budget & Reporting

  • Track and report key fleet metrics, including vehicle utilization, downtime, maintenance costs, fuel spend, accident and incident rates, and telematics safety scorecards.
  • Develop, monitor, and report on the fleet operating budget, partnering with Finance leadership to track costs against plan and identify variances.

Audits & Records Integrity

  • Perform regular audits of fleet records, including registrations, titles, insurance documentation, tags, and vehicle counts, to identify discrepancies and keep all systems and records current and accurate.
  • Support annual insurance audit reconciliation by ensuring vehicle counts and status records are up to date and consistent across all systems.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business, logistics, accounting, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.
  • 3 to 5+ years of experience in fleet management, transportation, or a related operations role.
  • Experience with Enterprise Fleet Management or a comparable fleet management platform required.
  • Experience with Geotab or a similar telematics and GPS tracking platform strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of commercial auto insurance processes, claims handling, DOT regulations, and DMV registration and titling requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to track, interpret, and report on fleet metrics, budgets, and KPIs.
  • Excellent organizational skills and a high level of attention to detail, with the ability to manage a high volume of records across multiple systems.
  • Strong communication and vendor management skills.
  • Expert data analysis skillswith heavy use Microsoft Excel, Tableau, and other Microsoft Office applications.
  • Certified Automotive Fleet Manager (CAFM) or similar fleet management certification a plus.

Benefits & Perks

At Marmic Fire and Safety, we offer more than just competitive pay. As a full-time employee, you'll enjoy a range of great benefits, including the below. Join us and enjoy a rewarding career with excellent perks!

  • Employee Ownership Program
  • Company-paid training programs and on-the-job training.
  • Tele-health services if healthcare coverage is elected
  • 401K plan with up to a 4% company match
  • Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance effective the first of the month following your start date
  • Accrual of up to 13 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) in your first year
  • 7 Paid Holidays annually

Who We Are

Since 1951, Marmic has focused on one mission: protecting the communities we serve. What began as a small, family-run fire protection business has grown into a trusted national partner for complete fire and life safety services. With 1,300+ team members and more than 50,000 customers, we deliver local, personal support backed by the strength and resources of a national organization.

As we’ve expanded - bringing more than 30 businesses into the Marmic family in just the past few years - we’ve built a culture where skilled technicians and industry experts can thrive, share their knowledge, and create lasting careers. We take pride in our work because it matters.

Every team member is also an owner of the company, sharing in the success they help create. That sense of ownership drives our culture of teamwork, accountability, and pride in craftsmanship. It also means our people are building a stronger financial future for themselves and their families.

Today, Marmic is one of the largest providers of comprehensive fire and life safety services in the country. Our teams install, inspect, and repair critical systems in industrial and corporate facilities, hospitals, schools, retail environments, and more—protecting lives and property every step of the way.

The Landline Company () is revolutionizing air travel by bridging the gap between regional communities and major airline hubs. We partner with top airlines like American Airlines and Air Canada to offer innovative multimodal connections across North America. We've launched a first of its kind remote terminal checkpoint to expand the reach of major metro airports into local neighborhoods. Our luxury motorcoaches replace short flights with a faster, more sustainable alternative in reducing costs, addressing pilot shortages, and enhancing passenger journeys.

Salary: 90,000 – 120,000

Job Type: Full Time, Salary Exempt

The Role: 
The Motorcoach Fleet Manager oversees Landline’s fleet management and maintenance functions. The role ensures the fleet is safe, clean, compliant, available, and maintained in accordance with OEM maintenance intervals, regulatory and Landline operational requirements. The Fleet Manager is the single point of contact for the Landline leadership team, maintenance business partners, OEMs, and our dispatch team.

The role will lead the maintenance function within Operations.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own the maintenance function at Landline with the plan, vendors and data for our fleet, with a path to scaling to support a 100-motorcoach fleet in the future
  • Build and maintain a rolling maintenance forecast aligned to OEM intervals and usage patterns, keeping every vehicle within OEM PM intervals
  • Maintain the maintenance budget with Finance, including updates and variance reporting
  • Coordinate unscheduled and corrective maintenance without disrupting service operations
  • Keep accurate service records in Fleetio and Samsara; track DVIR resolution and escalate out-of-service conditions to System Operations Control (SOC - Dispatch)
  • Manage parts and consumables procurement and validate pass-through costs from our maintenance partners
  • Flag recurring issues or vehicles approaching end of useful life using maintenance data
  • Serve as Landline's representative for all work at external maintenance facilities; issue work orders to fully utilize dedicated resources
  • Schedule all planned and unplanned work and ensure buses are positioned on time
  • Review and approve partner invoices, flag discrepancies, and track overflow technician usage against budget
  • Plan and conduct quarterly reviews with key maintenance vendors
  • Give the SOC and leadership a real-time view of fleet readiness (operational, in maintenance, or out of service) and communicate constraints proactively
  • Own Fleetio and Samsara as key user, including partner access and IT interfaces
  • Plan and manage vehicle assignments, identify capacity risks in advance, and support planning for additions, retirements, and configuration
  • Maintain vehicle files (registration, insurance, inspections, warranties)
  • Serve as primary contact with OEM reps; manage warranty claims and authorizations and coordinate technician training
  • Track Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs), service bulletins, and recalls and ensure timely action; advise leadership on OEM reliability and procurement
  • Provide the SOC advance notice of maintenance windows, report unplanned outages with return-to-service estimates, and collaborate on scheduling trade-offs
  • Ensure federal, state, and local compliance and timely inspections; keep audit-ready records and report KPIs (MTBF, out-of-service days, cost per vehicle)

  • Strong data and analytical skills (Excel required; SQL, Python, or BI tools like Tableau/Power BI a plus)
  • Familiarity with Fleetio and/or Samsara
  • Comfort using and recommending AI tools (e.g. Claude Code or similar) to move quickly across a diverse and shifting set of projects
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work with frontline hourly staff
  • A high-energy, self-directed approach and enthusiasm for solving operational problems in a fast-moving startup environment
  • Comfort working remotely while collaborating across multiple locations and time zones
  • The ability to think "bigger" than any single function as someone who understands the balancing act between commercial, finance, and operations, and can design solutions that serve the whole business rather than optimizing for one group at another's expense
  • Six Sigma certification (Green Belt, Black Belt, etc.) is a nice-to-have
  • Comfort working remotely while collaborating across multiple locations and time zones

  • Paid time off
  • Flight benefits through our airline partners
  • Company-paid life insurance

Position Description

Tenna is searching for a Product Manager who will support our product vision and roadmap, while providing clear direction to a cross-functional team of Software/Hardware Engineers and Designers. As a Product Manager, you will work closely with Engineering to translate detailed concepts into features, requirements, and acceptance criteria. This role will own or contribute significantly to our Electronic Logging Device (ELD) and fleet compliance product line, working at the intersection of hardware, software, and federal regulatory requirements. If you are a creative problem solver, obsessed with capturing the voice of our customers, enjoy rolling up your sleeves to get the job done, and possess a passion for IoT and fleet compliance technology – this might be the role for you.

Why Tenna?

At Tenna, we believe the best is right in front of all of us, and that each day holds more potential than the one before. We believe that every new discovery can lead to something better than we thought possible. When we boil it down, the top five qualities that define the Tenna Team are quality-obsessed, gritty, continuous learners, collaborative problem solvers, and just plain awesome. Sound like you? Join us as we empower our customers to control their mixed assets anytime, anywhere, on one comprehensive platform. Apply now!

Your Responsibilities

  • Leads and manages the entire feature and product lifecycle from planning, development, and launch.
  • Manages the iterative lifecycle of our product from idea conception to production including scope, defining specifications, prioritization, design, implementation, user acceptance testing, quality assurance, deployment, and maintenance.
  • Owns the product roadmap for ELD and Hours of Service (HOS) compliance features, ensuring the platform stays current with FMCSA ELD mandate requirements and other applicable federal and state regulations.
  • Creates product specifications as needed: wireframes with support from Design, process workflows, state transition diagrams, copy decks, acceptance test plans, user stories and acceptance criteria, and personas.
  • Defines and prioritizes the product backlog translating high-level requirements into user stories, and performs acceptance testing on a rolling basis throughout each product iteration.
  • Partners with Engineering and hardware/telematics teams to ensure ELD device connectivity, data accuracy, and compliance workflows (HOS logs, DVIRs, IFTA reporting) meet regulatory and customer requirements.
  • Champions our product internally and externally by pushing for rapid adoption.
  • Defines clear goals and KPIs around customer value and drives strategies to achieve them.
  • Captures the voice of our customers by actively engaging in end-user research, understanding end-user goals and pain points, and communicating key conclusions/takeaways to internal stakeholders — including drivers, fleet safety managers, and compliance officers.
  • Analyzes quantitative data to determine the most successful strategies and identify new product opportunities.
  • Assesses and makes creative recommendations on business opportunities for improvement in automation and efficiency of our processes.
  • Works closely with Design, and Development to define Product Vision, Roadmap, and Release Plans.
  • Ensures end-user adoption and identifies and measures user utility.
  • Collaborates with Marketing, Customer Success, and other internal stakeholders to define and execute go-to-market activities.
  • Monitors regulatory changes from FMCSA and other governing bodies, translating updates into product requirements ahead of compliance deadlines.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years' experience in an analytical, product-focused role.
  • 5+ years' experience delivering products as a Product Manager.
  • 2+ years' experience writing user stories and defining epics.
  • Prior experience writing or understanding code is strongly preferred.
  • Experience working in a B2B SaaS environment is strongly preferred.
  • Experience managing ELD (Electronic Logging Device) products or features strongly preferred, including familiarity with the FMCSA ELD mandate, Hours of Service (HOS) regulations, and related compliance workflows (DVIR, IFTA).
  • Experience within the construction technology, fleet management, or IoT industry is strongly preferred.
  • Experience bringing technology products to market in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proven ability to creatively solve problems, influence product improvements, and interpret business/technical requirements.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Design, Information Technology, Economics, or related STEM degree program is required or equivalent.
  • Ability to develop clean and targeted documentation, including process flows and standard operating procedures.
  • Strong analytical thinking and decision-making abilities.
  • Proven ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical people, including regulatory and compliance stakeholders.
